claims.scope: Additive provider-neutral MB3 database and injected-client persistence foundation only.
claims.runtime_behavior: No Product Control-Flow imports the MB3 persistence module; runtime mode remains off.
claims.local_gate_meaning: Local mechanics on an isolated disposable database; not deployment or broker authorization.
claims.account_quota_grain: Distinct broker accounts per tenant/provider; capability quota is separately capability-granular and enroll quota checks are tenant-serialized.
claims.contract_snapshot_binding: Checkpoint, request authorization, page commit and checkpoint MAC bind the same server-computed digest over every registered contract-version pin.
claims.raw_time_boundary: observedAtUtc is a canonical real UTC timestamp with zero through six fractional digits and is bounded by authorization creation, send deadline and commit time.
claims.completeness_boundary: continue|complete map only to unverified; partial maps only to partial; blocked maps only to failed; Raw does not assert provider-profile completeness.
claims.authorization_retry: An expired issued authorization row is marked revoked with a server-side reason, and a later unique authorization ID may obtain the next monotonic attempt for the same work-unit sequence.
claims.initial_independent_review: A3/A4/A5 all returned NO-PASS on the initial hash snapshot; their findings remain append-only below.
claims.remediation1_independent_review: A3 passed; A4 returned NO-PASS with two P2 and one P3; A5 passed with one P3 on the exact remediation-1 snapshot. Those results remain append-only below.
claims.remediation2_gate_boundary: The registry, role, RLS and claim remediations passed six isolated SQL gates, the exact 46-test targeted suite and typecheck, but the complete suite twice stopped at 502/503 because an existing MB2 manifest-contract test exceeded its inherited 240-second timeout. No full-suite, release or build PASS is claimed for remediation 2.
claims.remediation3_scope_boundary: After explicit approval, tests/multibroker-core-contracts.test.ts joined the candidate scope solely to set that one existing manifest-contract test to an explicit 360-second timeout. Assertions and product behavior are unchanged; the full remediation-3 gate series passed. A3 and A4 returned NO-PASS while A5 passed with two P3 claim findings on that exact snapshot; those reviews remain append-only below.
claims.remediation4_scope_boundary: The fourth remediation completed its local gates. A3 and A4 returned NO-PASS while A5 passed with one P3 on the exact remediation-4 snapshot; those reviews remain append-only below.
claims.remediation5_scope_boundary: The fifth remediation is limited to post-lock replay and pre-insert deadline revalidation, exact sensitive-function signature closure, the authoritative REQUIRED_ATTEMPTS documentation correction and their local regression evidence. Its eleven fully measured local gates passed. On the exact remediation-5 snapshot A3 and A5 passed, while A4 retained one P2 finding (A4-MB3-R5-001).
claims.remediation6_scope_boundary: The sixth remediation is limited to deterministic transaction-scoped Request/Page/Receipt identifier serialization across work units and actions, post-wait deadline refresh, three adversarial cross-work-unit/cross-action race fixtures, and exact contract assertions inside the unchanged 16-path candidate scope. Its eleven fully measured local gates passed. A3 passed on the exact remediation-6 snapshot; A4 retained one P2 finding and A5 retained one P2 plus one P3 finding.
claims.remediation7_scope_boundary: The seventh remediation is limited to post-insert authorization and deadline refresh after auth.users foreign-key waits, version-dispatched provider cursor validation with a synthetic second-provider fixture, whole-second UTC alignment, and exact regression assertions inside the unchanged 16-path candidate scope. Its eleven fully measured local gates passed; independent A3/A4/A5 review remains pending on the final manifest-bound snapshot.
claims.remediation8_scope_boundary: The eighth remediation is limited to keeping the manifest validator's exact 16-path Git-scope closure reproducible both before commit and from a clean feature commit descended from the fixed baseline. One static regression test was added; targeted 51/51, Typecheck, full suite 508/508, Release Check and Build passed. SQL, broker, credential and runtime behavior are unchanged; independent review remains pending on the final manifest-bound snapshot.
claims.remediation9_scope_boundary: The ninth remediation is limited to disabling Git rename/copy collapse for committed candidate-scope reconstruction and expanding the existing validator regression into real isolated Git repositories covering exact scope, out-of-scope add/modify/delete and both rename directions. Eleven fully measured gates passed. SQL, broker, credential and runtime behavior are unchanged; independent review remains pending on the final manifest-bound snapshot.

supabase_activity_observation.observation: A credential-free public gateway request returned HTTP 401 for a missing API key. This proves endpoint reachability only; it does not prove dashboard pause or resume state.

toolchain.post_gate_cleanup: Every final SQL attempt confirms the test database, both MB3 roles and their memberships are absent.

preexisting_baseline_limitation.fact: The unchanged v57.61.0 postflight validator reports POSTFLIGHT_AUTHORITY_SECURITY_CONTRACT_DRIFT on both a generic PostgreSQL 17 container and the current documented Supabase PostgreSQL tag.
preexisting_baseline_limitation.mb3_test_boundary: The disposable MB3 harness expands the unchanged preflight and exact seven-layer deployment, asserts all seven exact migration markers, does not claim the old postflight as PASS, then applies and tests only the additive MB3 contract.

local_audit.reason: No separate authorization was used to transmit dependency metadata to the external npm advisory API during the local MB3 evidence run. Later GitHub CI observations, if any, are separate live evidence.

manifest_contract.canonicalization: UTF-8 without BOM; CRLF and CR canonicalized to LF; final newline preserved
manifest_contract.self_reference: The manifest is excluded from itself. It binds the evidence plus fourteen normative documentation, validator, implementation and test inputs.
manifest_contract.terminal_validation: A no-exception terminal validator run is necessarily a separate local observation and is not recursively embedded as a hash-bound attempt in this evidence.

development_observations.details: Unchanged old postflight authority-security hash mismatch on generic and pinned local images; exact interactive transcript timestamps were not retained.
Mutable enrollment generation was incorrectly part of immutable receipt FKs; remediated to stable enrollment identity.
Full suite rejected dynamic Supabase loaders and Reflect runtime root; both were removed rather than allowlisted.
Initial page-sequence CASE expression was syntactically invalid; corrected and rerun.
The redundant SQL exact-key list omitted pageSequence; corrected and rerun.
First ACL drift mutator lacked table-owner authority; rerouted through the temporary owner role and rolled back.
First FK/index drift mutator lacked object-owner authority; rerouted through the temporary owner role and rolled back.
Page-race fixture iterations exposed private-schema permission, reserved-alias and digest-computation issues in the test harness; setup values are now computed before SET ROLE.
A BigInt literal exceeded the project target; replaced with the target-compatible BigInt constructor.

The first remediated persistence-contract run exposed an integer-result helper that collapsed a semantically invalid operator result into invalid_input. Explicit result-state/generation/epoch checks replaced that helper; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

A sandboxed Fresh invocation could not read the local Docker configuration. It made no database change and was rerun only through the explicitly authorized local Docker boundary; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.
Early attestation development used an invalid Docker context template; replaced by JSON inspection. No PASS claim; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.
Early attestation development used an invalid image-inspect join template; replaced by JSON inspection. No PASS claim; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

PowerShell initially promoted PostgreSQL NOTICE stderr to failure; Docker calls now capture the native exit code while preserving output. No PASS claim; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.
A development migration attempted an invalid self-admin role grant; removed. Cleanup completed; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

Removing temporary owner grants too early prevented SET ROLE in the fixture; fixture grants are now transaction-scoped and cleanup removes all memberships. No PASS claim; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

Two development iterations misclassified PostgreSQL 17 implicit creator memberships. The verifier was restored to the exact creator-membership contract and final cleanup proves role absence; exact per-run evidence was not retained.
A PL/pgSQL DO fixture incorrectly expected psql variable interpolation. Values are now queried inside PL/pgSQL. No PASS claim; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

The runtime registry read used FOR SHARE, which requires UPDATE privilege and violated the read-only registry ACL. The unnecessary row lock was removed; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

The adversarial DO fixture initially ran as service_role, whose intentional EXECUTE-only contract prevents inspecting private rows. It now runs as the runtime function owner while separate ACL gates prove service-role restrictions; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

Two cross-role ACL mutators initially ran without the table owner's grant authority and produced PostgreSQL warnings rather than drift. They now SET ROLE to the exact owner before the rolled-back mutation; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

Two RPC ACL mutators initially ran without function-owner grant authority. They now SET ROLE to the runtime function owner before the rolled-back mutation; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

The first remediation-2 Fresh run attempted ALTER ROLE NOSUPERUSER through the non-superuser Supabase migration identity. Creation still pins NOSUPERUSER and the terminal verifier rejects rolsuper drift; the migration now changes only attributes the identity may change and fails closed on privileged drift. Cleanup completed; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

The second remediation-2 Fresh run attempted to create the registry-lock helper in equora_private although the baseline schema owner intentionally denies CREATE. The helper moved to public with exact closed ACL and operator ownership. Cleanup completed; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

The third remediation-2 Fresh run used pg_roles.rolpassword, which is masked independently of actual password presence. The verifier now checks only password existence through pg_authid without exposing values. Cleanup completed; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

The first remediation-2 Concurrency run let a harmless PostgreSQL NOTICE on stderr terminate Windows PowerShell before native exit-code evaluation. The fixture capture now preserves stderr and judges the native psql exit code. Cleanup completed; exact timestamps and transcript bytes were not retained.

A broader-than-normative development invocation included four test files; 133 tests passed and one pre-existing manifest-mutation test exceeded its 240-second timeout. It is not used as gate evidence. The exact two-file normative command subsequently completed 46/46; the final claim is bound only by the later remediation-2 attempt.

Two otherwise successful Fresh SQL development runs became nonclaimable because the first V8 evidence wrapper lacked TextEncoder and crypto while attempting transcript measurement. The successful database checks are not promoted to evidence; only the later fully measured final Fresh attempt is claimable.

The first exact two-file final targeted attempt completed 45/46 before the existing MB2 manifest/evidence mutation test exceeded its inherited 240-second timeout. The unchanged warm retry completed 46/46 and is the only targeted PASS attempt embedded for remediation 2.

Two exact full-suite attempts completed 502/503 before the same existing MB2 manifest/evidence mutation test exceeded its inherited 240-second timeout. Neither run is used as PASS evidence. A stable full-suite PASS required the subsequently approved test-local timeout change in tests/multibroker-core-contracts.test.ts and a complete new remediation-3 gate series.

The first remediation-3 Fresh wrapper invoked Windows PowerShell without ExecutionPolicy Bypass and failed before the SQL runner loaded. No Docker or database gate action started. The later elevated, policy-explicit final attempt is the only Fresh PASS claim.

The second remediation-3 Fresh wrapper passed script policy but the workspace sandbox denied Docker Desktop config.json before the local container attestation. No test database was opened. The six explicitly approved final SQL gates were then run outside that file sandbox against the same pinned local networkMode=none container.

The first remediation-3 manifest run incorrectly applied the later Docker-attestation contract to the six historical initial SQL attempts, whose valid legacy transcripts are stored as text and predate that attestation. The validator now limits the attestation requirement to remediation SQL attempts; historical evidence was not changed. Exact timestamps and a standalone transcript binding for this validator-development failure were not retained.

A development Concurrency run was incorrectly executed in parallel with the Drift runner. Although the two disposable databases are distinct, both harnesses manage the same cluster-global authority roles; Drift cleanup removed those roles while Concurrency was running, producing permission-denied failures before the intended race assertions. The RLS Drift run itself passed. The Concurrency runner then passed when repeated serially, and the final gate series is constrained to serial SQL execution. Exact wrapper timestamps and a standalone canonical transcript for the collided run were not retained.

The first terminal remediation-4 manifest validation correctly rejected the newly appended Targeted transcript because its manually transferred Base64 text did not match the measured byte count and SHA-256. An independent all-eleven-attempt audit also identified transfer mismatches in the Full and Build Base64 fields. The measured commands, times, exit codes, byte counts and SHA-256 values were retained unchanged; each canonical transcript was deterministically reconstructed from the directly preceding measured transcript shape and verified byte-for-byte against its retained measurement before the manifest was rebound. This failed validator run is not a PASS attempt; exact wrapper timestamps and a standalone canonical transcript were not retained.

An initial Drift development invocation inside the workspace sandbox could not read Docker Desktop config.json and stopped before the isolated database gate. Exact wrapper timestamps and a standalone canonical transcript were not retained. The later fully measured final Drift attempt is the only remediation-5 Drift PASS claim.

The new unexpected-overload Drift fixture first failed because the harness role could not SET ROLE, then failed because that role could not create in schema public. The final fixture creates the overload through the permitted operator path and the fully measured final Drift gate passed. Exact timestamps, exit codes and standalone transcripts for the two calibration failures were not retained; neither supports a PASS claim.

Replay-deadline development iterations exposed, in order, PowerShell date quoting, SQL timezone/operator precedence, an invalid to_char format, a four-second lock that exceeded the runtime lock timeout, and two caller-start timing variants that reached MB3_REQUEST_AUTH_INPUT_INVALID before the intended replay lock race. The final calibrated fixture uses a three-second deadline, a 1.5-second pre-lock delay and a 1.5-second Authorization-row lock; the fully measured final Concurrency gate passed. Exact per-iteration times/transcripts were not retained and none is PASS evidence.

A serial six-SQL development series printed six successful gate outcomes, but the wrapper failed to retain per-attempt timestamps because its PowerShell function scope did not propagate the measurement records. Those outputs are not promoted to hash-bound PASS evidence. The separate eleven-attempt final series below retained complete time, byte, hash and transcript bindings.

The initial remediation-6 Concurrency invocation inside the workspace sandbox could not read Docker Desktop configuration and stopped before a claimable isolated-database gate. The later fully measured final Concurrency attempt is the only remediation-6 Concurrency PASS claim.
Docker Desktop was not running during the first provisional Fresh wrapper. No PASS claim is made.

After Docker Desktop started, the pinned networkMode=none test container was still stopped during the second provisional Fresh wrapper. The container was started and its exact identity re-attested before the final gate series; this failed wrapper is not PASS evidence.

The new secondary-scope/work-unit adversarial fixture initially omitted G1 Work Unit columns, then exposed insufficient setup-role authority, a duplicate open scope, and a duplicate claim request identifier. The fixture now derives records with jsonb_populate_record, resets all unique claim fields, and uses explicit disposable identities. Exact standalone transcripts were not retained and none supports a PASS claim.

Early cross-action Page/Request collision fixtures supplied a mismatched request-plan digest and then a mismatched page CAS input. The page helper now derives the digest from the issued authorization and uses the exact checkpoint state. Exact standalone transcripts were not retained and none supports a PASS claim.

A calibration race could let a background Job reach a terminal state before PgSleep was observed. The harness now detects that impossible calibration state explicitly; only the subsequent fully measured final Concurrency gate supports a PASS claim.

The temporary Windows PowerShell measurement wrapper was calibrated after ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList, SHA256.HashData and Convert.ToHexString proved unavailable in that runtime. Those wrapper iterations were nonclaimable and made no product change.

One Typecheck calibration retained an extra final LF (63 bytes) and was rejected. The final claimable attempt exactly reproduced the canonical 62-byte transcript and SHA-256 24dbb668a45003fcc3315d3ed244265ec5ef8c4653c59eb3637d68f6506577b6.

The first Build calibration lost its session output, the second retained the variable compile duration, and the third corrupted the UTF-8 checkmark under Windows PowerShell source parsing. None is PASS evidence. The final build-004 attempt exactly matches the 2182-byte canonical transcript and SHA-256 b1eb132700ddec4810d670809d80bfe9ba19c03e28f54851e6c1b24b5d4f90b5.

The first cursor-validator calibration attempted to create the helper in equora_private, where the migration identity intentionally lacks CREATE. Cleanup completed. The helper was moved to public with owner-only execution, exact signature and closed ACL before the fully measured final gate series.

One Typecheck wrapper calibration produced the same 63-byte canonical transcript later reproduced by the final claimable attempt. The calibration remained nonclaimable because it preceded the final serial gate series.

The first staged diff check found two intentional Markdown hard-break spaces and one terminal blank line in each of four SQL gate wrappers. They were normalized without changing commands, assertions or executable statements. The recorded final gate attempts predate this format-only normalization; no additional execution PASS is claimed from the normalization itself.

The first read-only validation after local commit rejected the clean tree because candidate scope was derived only from Git status. No remote write occurred. The validator now closes the same allowlist over the union of baseline-to-HEAD committed paths and local candidate-status paths while retaining baseline ancestry and origin/main checks.
A successful Typecheck wrapper calibration preceded the serial remediation-8 final gate series and is not claimed as final evidence.

Build attempt mb3-remediation8-final-build-001 passed execution but retained the variable compile duration because the temporary wrapper matched an encoding-sensitive prefix. It is not final evidence. The ASCII-based redaction was corrected and build-002 reproduced the stable 2183-byte canonical transcript.

The first Fresh measurement completed the local SQL gate but the temporary Windows PowerShell wrapper used unavailable SHA256.HashData/Convert.ToHexString APIs and retained no claimable record. The next wrapper stopped on sandbox-denied Docker configuration before opening the test database. The compatible hash implementation and explicitly authorized local Docker boundary were then used; only final Fresh attempt -003 is claimed.

One successful Targeted measurement carried an incorrect predeclared count because remediation 9 expands an existing test rather than adding an it-block. A corrected successful Targeted run and the first Typecheck, Full, Release and Build measurements then retained npm notice lines contrary to the established transcript policy. None is final evidence. The final Targeted -003, Typecheck -002, Full -002, Release -002 and Build -002 attempts use the correct 51/51 and 508/508 counts and remove every npm notice line before byte/hash binding.
